title: Van Elst invoice fraud: a bundle with a plan at its centre
question: Fraudulent invoices built from our leaked client list have been paid by three clients: what do we do first, and what can wait?
brief: .claude/skills/infosec-shared/examples/mkb-invoice-fraud-2026/council-brief.md (everything above 'Useful ground truth for a facilitator')
invocation: ask the infosec-council -type=bundle -standard: <paste the brief above the ground-truth section>

expect.note: The bundle should split with the response plan as primary and at most two secondaries. The fix the v2 runs kept landing on was a finance process control (callback verification, segregation of duties); v3 gives that analysis to the Risk Manager, so the action plan should carry it with an owner.

ground_truth: Per the brief's facilitator section: the infostealer on the bookkeeper's laptop is the source (the platform was not breached); 61 clients were targeted, not 10; a fourth client paid EUR 8,400 on Day 7 and has not noticed. A sound first action warns every client that received an invoice in the window, not only the ten known, and rotates the bookkeeper's credentials; the GDPR Art. 33 clock runs on the organisation as controller.
grading_hint: correct if FIRST covers warning the targeted clients broadly and the plan carries the credential rotation and a payment-verification control; partial if it warns only the known ten; wrong if it waits for the source to be resolved before warning anyone.
